events.title: Galileo Recants Before the Inquisition
events.description: In Rome, Galileo Galilei was forced by the Roman Catholic Inquisition to formally abjure his support for the Copernican heliocentric model, which held that the Earth orbits the Sun. He was sentenced to house arrest for the rest of his life.
events.significance: The trial became a lasting symbol of the conflict between scientific inquiry and institutional authority, and it shaped later debates about freedom of thought and the relationship between science and religion.

events.title: Chesapeake–Leopard Affair
events.description: The British warship HMS Leopard attacked and boarded the American frigate USS Chesapeake off the coast of Virginia, seeking deserters from the Royal Navy. Three American sailors were killed and four were taken off the ship.
events.significance: The incident inflamed American public opinion against Britain over impressment and naval rights, contributing to tensions that led to the Embargo Act of 1807 and ultimately the War of 1812.

events.title: U.S. Department of Justice Established
events.description: President Ulysses S. Grant signed legislation creating the United States Department of Justice, with the Attorney General as its head, to handle the federal government's legal business and enforce federal law.
events.significance: The Department became the central federal law enforcement and legal institution of the United States, and was used early on to prosecute Ku Klux Klan violence during Reconstruction.

events.title: Germany Invades the Soviet Union (Operation Barbarossa)
events.description: Nazi Germany and its Axis allies launched a massive surprise invasion of the Soviet Union along a front stretching from the Baltic to the Black Sea, breaking the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact of 1939. It involved roughly three million German troops and became the largest invasion in military history.
events.significance: The invasion opened the Eastern Front, the largest and deadliest theater of World War II, and ultimately contributed greatly to Germany's defeat while bringing the Soviet Union into the Allied camp.

events.title: Cuyahoga River Fire
events.description: Oil and debris floating on the heavily polluted Cuyahoga River in Cleveland, Ohio, caught fire. The blaze was relatively small and quickly extinguished, but it drew national attention after Time magazine covered it.
events.significance: The fire became an iconic image of industrial pollution and helped spur the American environmental movement, contributing to the creation of the EPA in 1970 and the passage of the Clean Water Act in 1972.
